The first Arab mission to another planet, the Al Amal, or “Hope,” probe will capture the first comprehensive picture of the Martian climate. Thanks to its around-the-clock monitoring, the global science community will have the opportunity to study the relationship between Mars' current and ancient climates and investigate how atmospheres change over time. Almost as impressive as humanity's ability to send a probe 37 million miles to Mars and the unprecedented data that this mission will collect is the fact that the woman spearheading the scientific mission on this project, Her Excellency Sarah Al Amiri, has barely embarked on her 30s. The Hiligaynon language of the central Philippines is filled with mouthwatering onomatopoeia. There’s lagting (scraping and tapping cutlery), tamsak (smacking lips) and harakhak (cackling laughter). But the word that comes to mind as I tuck in to a brioche bun filled with ginamos , a pungent paste made from fish or shrimps, is mananam (umami). pages.text: Meet the Salak, the Ubiquitous Indonesian Fruit You’ve Never Heard Of Skip to main content Monsaro’s snakefruit, freshly plucked from a nearby village. Photo by Rachel Nuwer At a morning market in Bali, the usual gaudy suspects – papayas, mangos, dragon fruit and heaps of rancid-smelling durians - are on display. For Western visitors seeking culinary novelty, however, the most enticing fruit likely will not be the biggest or the brightest, but a humble, shiny brown offering called the salak. For the uninitiated, this fleshy, spongey morsel offers a perfumed cocktail of bright flavors, with hints of pineapple, citrus, honey and possibly even soap. In Indonesia, salaks are as common as apples or oranges in the U.S. Also called snakefruit, this strawberry-sized, fig-shaped fruit comes encased in vivid, nutty-brown scales, not unlike that of a cobra or python. Heaps of salaks turn up daily at countless local markets, while touristy hotels offer them up in breakfast buffet lines as examples of typical island fare. The odd but ubiquitous morsels can be boiled with sugar into a sweet spread , pickled , vacuum dried and fried into chips or paired with other fruits and nuts , but locals prefer them best raw and straight off the tree. pages.text: Meet the ‘giant’ river crabs that live beneath Rome’s ancient ruins | National Geographic By Asia London Palomba Published June 27, 2024 During excavations of Trajan’s Forum in central Rome in 2005, archaeologists found an ancient sewer drain that contained a marble bust of Constantine dating to the 4th century A.D . and a population of river crabs with an even older heritage. Freshwater crabs of the species ( Potamon fluviatile ) inhabit burrows in rivers and streams across Italy (one shown in Tuscany). Photograph By Emanuele Biggi Overwhelmed by the crabs, archaeologists hauled buckets of them out of the earth during excavations. Known scientifically as Potamon fluviatile , these crustaceans are the only large freshwater crabs indigenous to Italy. Researchers suspect that the population’s heritage is ancient, dating back to when Rome wasn’t much more than a marshy valley. ( Two Vampire Crab Species Found, Are Already Popular Pets) The crustaceans have not been extensively studied and have been largely forgotten about over the last 15 years. These crabs may have seen empires rise and fall, but new monitoring data suggest that this once plentiful population could be at risk of disappearing. ( Pictures: New Purple Crab Species Found) How ancient are these crabs? Unsurprisingly, the crabs’ habitat has changed significantly over the last 2,000 years. Taxodium Lawn is a popular picnic spot in Melbourne’s Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria, established in 1846 on the south bank of the Yarra River. Wim Wiskerke, Alamy By Justin Meneguzzi Published October 20, 2026 A 19th-century gold rush made Melbourne one of the wealthiest places on earth, bringing waves of migration and investment that still shape its modern identity. Today, the city’s riches can be found in modernist art galleries, divey comedy clubs, and bluestone laneways with hidden cafés. The culinary scene is electric and eclectic, with Ethiopian, Korean, Filipino, and Italian restaurants often sitting side by side on the same street. Add an ambitious plan to “green” the city with a dozen new parks and an expanded train network, and there are more reasons to visit the capital of Victoria than ever before. pages.text: Melissa Aldana and Gonzalo Rubalcaba talk jazz : Alt.Latino : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Melissa Aldana and Gonzalo Rubalcaba talk jazz : Alt.Latino Jazz has often been called America's musical gift to the world. This week's guests remind us not only of the well-documented ways that Cuba revolutionized that gift, but also how it blossomed in South America. Chilean tenor saxophonist Melissa Aldana and Cuban pianist Gonzalo Rubalcaba stopped by after their recent Tiny Desk performance to chat about their own personal histories with jazz and its lineage in their respective countries. The memories Rubalcaba shares about Havana's jazz scene in the 1980s adds another layer to a story we've talked a lot about on Alt.Latino. And Aldana looks back on her youth learning music from her father and grandfather, both of whom were Chilean jazz pioneers. The conversation also covers the music they played at the Tiny Desk, which comes from their recent album, 'Filin,' a reexamination of a Cuban musical movement that lasted from the 1940s through the '60s. Ultimately, this week's episode is time spent with two master musicians to hear how their lives and experiences contribute to their mutual appreciation and love of jazz. Melissa Klembara Melissa Klembara is Deputy Director for the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations (OCED) at the U.S. Department of Energy. In this role, she leads programs that accelerate the deployment of advanced energy and manufacturing technologies, supporting the Department’s mission to drive innovation and economic growth across the United States. With more than 20 years of public-sector experience, Klembara has managed multi-billion-dollar portfolios and spearheaded strategic initiatives that unlock private-sector investment and foster innovation across the U.S. industrial and energy landscape. Her leadership has been instrumental in advancing the commercialization of innovative technologies and strengthening public-private partnerships. Prior to her current role, Klembara served as Director of Portfolio Strategy at OCED, overseeing the design and execution of commercial and pilot-scale demonstrations. Klembara is recognized for her expertise in strategy and program management, cross-sector collaboration, and advancing the scale-up of innovative technologies that drive economic benefits for the U.S. She led DOE’s Pathways to Commercial Liftoff report series for OCED, covering topics such as advanced nuclear, industrial, and hydrogen

pages.description: As climate change warms the planet, more discoveries of human remains and objects in ice are expected to occur
pages.text: Melting Swiss Glacier Reveals Remains of Climber Who Disappeared in 1986 Skip to main content Mountaineers came upon the gear and remains of a hiker missing since 1986 last month. Cantonal Police of Valais Mountaineers trekking along a glacier in Switzerland have made a surprising discovery: the body and equipment of a hiker who had been missing for nearly 40 years. On July 12, the group was traveling across Theodul Glacier in Zermatt, Switzerland, not far from the famous Matterhorn mountain, when they stumbled upon pieces of gear and human remains, per a statement from the local police. Authorities sent the remains for DNA testing at Valais Hospital, which revealed that the newly discovered body belonged to a German mountain climber who had gone missing in September 1986. The police did not share the deceased individual’s name, but they said the mountaineer was 38 years old in 1986. At the time, search teams tried to find the hiker but were ultimately unsuccessful. It’s not clear how or why the German alpinist died, nor the conditions that made it impossible for the person to return home safely. However, discoveries like this one may become more and more common amid rising global temperatures, as glaciers like Theodul continue to melt. “The retreat of the glaciers brings to light an increasing number of missing alpinists who were reported missing several decades ago,” police said in the statement. Memorandum of Understanding Between EPA and OSHA for Implementation of TSCA Section 6 In December 2024, EPA and the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) of the U.S. Department of Labor entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) formalizing their coordination on EPA’s work to assess and manage existing chemicals under section 6 of the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA). EPA and OSHA anticipate that better coordination under this MOU will result in improved workplace health and safety protections for workers using existing chemical substances under TSCA and the Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Act and allow for effective implementation of national workplace and environmental protection statutes. Meningococcal Disease and People Receiving Complement Inhibitors Mar. 6, 2026 Español Key points Receiving a complement inhibitor greatly increases someone's risk of meningococcal disease. Getting vaccinated and taking antibiotics offers some (but not complete) protection. People receiving complement inhibitors should seek treatment quickly for symptoms of meningococcal disease. Be aware that prompt treatment is important even for those who've been vaccinated or who are taking antibiotics. Complement inhibitors greatly increase risk Compared to otherwise healthy people, someone receiving a complement inhibitor is up to 2,000 times more likely to get meningococcal disease. Meningococcal disease is often serious and can be deadly. Meningococcal Disease in Other Countries Mar. 16, 2026 Key points Meningococcal disease occurs worldwide. The highest incidence of meningococcal disease is found in the 'meningitis belt' of sub-Saharan Africa. Other regions of the world experience lower overall rates of disease and occasional outbreaks. Learn about global trends in meningococcal disease. Meningitis belt The meningitis belt of sub-Saharan African historically experienced major epidemics of meningococcal disease every 5 to 12 years. Attack rates during these epidemics reached up to 1,000 cases per 100,000 population. Risk factors for meningococcal disease outbreaks in Africa aren't fully understood. However, the following characteristics create favorable conditions for meningococcal disease epidemics: Dry, dusty conditions during the dry season (December to June) Immunological susceptibility of the population Travel and large population displacements Crowded living conditions Vaccine impact Historically, outbreaks in the meningitis belt were primarily due to serogroup A meningococcal disease. December 20, 2024 Meningococcal Vaccine Safety Key points There are two types of vaccines that can prevent meningococcal disease. Overview Meningococcal disease can refer to any illness that is caused by a type of bacteria called Neisseria meningitidis , also known as meningococcus. N. meningitidis is a leading cause of bacterial meningitis in children ages 2 through 18 years in the United States. There are six serogroups (a group of bacteria that are closely related) of N. meningitidis that cause most meningococcal disease in the world. They are referred to as serogroups A, B, C, W, X, and Y. Available vaccines & manufacturer package inserts MenACWY Also known as quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccines. Protects against meningococcal disease caused by serogroups A, C, W, and Y. pages.description: Long before the Roman Empire, Talayotic people left their mark in wondrous stone structures on the Spanish island.
pages.text: Menorca’s ‘houses of the dead’ reveal these ancient secrets | National Geographic By Eva van den Berg Published July 28, 2022 • 15 min read From atop Menorca’s megalithic stone towers, watchers would have witnessed the tides of history roll across the island with the successive waves of the ancient Mediterranean superpowers—the Phoenicians, Greeks, and Romans. But long before those heavyweights stepped ashore, the island’s humble pioneers carved out a life on the windswept, largely treeless landscape. Those towers, called talayots , were built from the raw material those first inhabitants and their descendants found in abundance—blocks of limestone. By simply making do with what they had, the Menorcans created a legacy set in stone. To most, Spain ’s Balearic Islands may be better known for the jet-set beach destinations of Ibiza and Mallorca. But tranquil Menorca, the easternmost link in the chain, combines that natural beauty with a unique treasure trove—the archipelago’s greatest repository of ancient architecture. Within these towers and other “ cyclopean ” structures—made from unhewn, mortarless stones—lies an island history knit together over a millennium, leaving its mark on the Menorcan landscape and identity. Menorca is home to almost 400 talayots, towers for which the Talayotic culture is named. Researchers believe the structures were probably used as watch towers or for defense, though their function is still subject to debate. Photograph: Eurovision Song Contest Asia Eurovision Mesh masks, Nana’s lampshade and the other Beck: what to watch for at Eurovision Asia The first ever Eurovision Asia song contest takes place in Thailand on Saturday, and it won’t disappoint those hoping for some bizarre acts Martin Belam Sat 14 Nov 2026 07.00 EST Last modified on Sat 14 Nov 2026 07.04 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google T he first ever Eurovision Asia is being held in Thailand on Saturday. The event is a more compact affair than the European version has become, and with only 11 countries competing, it isn’t a straightforward cultural import. None of the entrants have gone near wacky Eurovision vibes such as having a singing turkey or banana-eating wolves . Restrictive attitudes to homosexuality in some of the countries where the show will be broadcast have also tempered the overt campness and LGBTQ+ representation with which Eurovision has come to be associated – there will certainly not be an equivalent of Olly Alexander getting sweaty in a grubby gym changing room . Some habits die hard, however: when singing to an international audience, nearly half the entries still lean on English lyrics. Instead, they tell a story of strategic investment, scientific resilience, and an unwavering commitment to the U.S. research community. Why Our Metrics Matter Today Scientific Continuity: Despite restricted reactor operations, our community has consistently produced over 200–300 publications annually. Modernizing for a 10x Leap: We are leveraging this period to upgrade 3 beamlines, build a new neutron spectrometer, upgrade 11 other instruments, and enhance multiple sample environments. It also offered an ominous warning of things to come. The picturesque Mexican city of Guadalajara is bustling with life. By day, its busy plazas are filled with street vendors and shoeshine boys. At night, the mariachis line up to play for the tourists. The country's drug violence feels very far from here and, most of the time, it is. But that was not always the case. "In 1985, Guadalajara was the base of operations for most of the major narcotics traffickers in North America," says James Kuykendall, then-head of the Guadalajara office of the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). "Many of the major traffickers from other parts of Mexico, especially the state of Sinaloa, had migrated to Guadalajara both for the scenery and for the politics: if they didn't have full immunity, certainly no-one was messing with them down there." Among the agents working out of the small office was a 37-year-old Mexican-born American, Enrique "Kiki" Camarena. pages.text: Mexico's Bread of the Dead Kneads Together Indigenous and Catholic Traditions Skip to main content Travel | October 30, 2026 Mexico’s Bread of the Dead Kneads Together Indigenous and Catholic Traditions Pan de Muerto, a Mexican sweet bread eaten for Día de los Muertos, is more than just a festive treat. Its history mirrors the holiday itself, a combination of cultures that breathes life back into the dead Pan de muerto is an orange-scented sweet bread traditionally prepared and eaten during Día de los Muertos , a Mexican holiday celebrated each year from October 31 to November 2. Eder Marcos Camacho Gomez/Getty Images Pan de muerto is an orange-scented sweet bread traditionally prepared and eaten during Día de los Muertos , a Mexican holiday celebrated each year from October 31 to November 2. Eder Marcos Camacho Gomez/Getty Images It’s autumn in Mexico City, and baker Elena Reygadas and her team at Panadería Rosetta are hard at work in the kitchen. Deftly, they shape mounds of soft, elastic dough into perfect rounds. Then, with two fingers, they gingerly form the huesitos , or little bones, laying the thin strips in a cross over the buns. A tray full of rolls slides into the bakery rack, resting alongside dozens of other matching loaves waiting for their turn in the oven. The bakers are making pan de muerto , an orange-scented sweet bread traditionally prepared and eaten during Día de los Muertos , Day of the Dead, a Mexican holiday celebrated each year from October 31 to November 2. For three days, legend decrees, the border between the mortal and spirit realms disappears.

Close michaelIsADullGuy's Diary 南京新街口地块精细化更新日志 Posted by michaelIsADullGuy on 29 May 2026 in Chinese (China) (‪中文(中国大陆)‬) . 前言 新街口作为南京乃至华东地区最重要的商业核心之一，其 OSM 数据长期存在建筑轮廓粗糙、地下空间缺失、路径拓扑混乱等问题。为此，我启动了一项针对新街口地块的系统性精细化更新计划，并在此记录操作步骤与我所制定的制图标准，供社区参考与讨论。 一、建筑物轮廓与属性细化 所有建筑物的轮廓均参照最新卫星影像与实地核查进行重新描绘或修正，具体标准如下： 轮廓贴合建筑基底，避免过度简化或偏移； 补充 building:levels 、 height 、 name 、 start_date 等属性； 对于综合体建筑（如德基广场、金鹰国际），区分裙楼与塔楼，分别以 building 、 building:part 进行三维建模。 二、地下商业空间的划定 新街口地铁站（地铁1号线×2号线换乘）向四周延伸出大量地下通道，直接连通周边各大商场的负一层。凡与地铁站地下通道 直接联通 的商场负一层空间，均按以下标准标注为地下建筑区域： 使用 location=underground 或 layer=-1 标记相关区域； 地下商业区域的范围多边形参照实际通道出入口与商业空间边界绘制； 与地铁站直接相连的通道本身，以 tunnel=yes + layer=-1 的 highway=footway 表示； 暂不确定是否联通的区域，暂以 fixme=需核实地下联通情况 标注，留待后续实地核查。 目前已完成地下空间划定的区域包括： 新街口百货商店 B1、金陵中环 B1 待补充区域： 金鹰国际购物中心 B1、德基广场 B1、中央商场 B1、南京国际金融中心 B1 等。 三、路径拓扑标准 这是本次更新中最容易出错的部分。为确保路网拓扑的清洁与导航规划的准确性，我制定了以下强制性规则： 3.1 各类道路不得混接 在主要路口， 行人路径（ highway=footway/pedestrian ）、自行车道（ highway=cycleway ）、机动车道（ highway=primary 等） 三者之间，原则上不建议建立直接连接节点，除非现实中存在明确的路权交汇点（如行人过街横道节点）。 3.2 跨图层要素禁止连接 任何两个 不属于同一 layer 值 的路径要素， 不得出现共享连接节点 ，以下情况除外： 允许连接的要素 说明 highway=steps 阶梯，连接不同楼层/层级 含 conveying=yes 的 highway=footway 自动扶梯 highway=elevator 电梯 除上述垂直交通要素外，地面路径与地下路径 一律不得出现连接点 。 此规则同样适用于在导航计算中看似”无害”的连接（例如建筑物轮廓与步行道路相切）。只要两个要素不属于同一图层，路径要素与非路径要素之间同样须保持几何上的独立性，仅在视觉上相邻即可。同一图层内的要素按正常规则连接，不受此限制。 如有异议或建议，欢迎在变更集评论或讨论页留言。 Happy mapping! 🗺️ Discussion Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

pages.text: Michelangelo and the Tomb that Tormented Him | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE Michelangelo and the Tomb that Tormented Him During his years in Rome, Michelangelo took on some of the Renaissance’s most important and difficult commissions—from the Sistine Chapel to St. Peter’s Basilica. But nothing burdened him more than the tomb of Pope Julius II. “Moses" by Michelangelo Created between 1513 and 1516, this sculpture became the centerpiece of Pope Julius II’s tomb when it was installed in 1545. Anna Serrano/Fototeca 9x12 By Eloi de Tera Published November 16, 2026 The warm torpor of summer still lingered in the long afternoons of September 1534, when momentous news reached Florence. Giulio de’ Medici, Pope Clement VII, had died on the 25th of that month, after allegedly eating poisonous mushrooms. The tomb of Giuliano de’ Medici, with figures “Night” and “Day,” was designed and sculpted by Michelangelo. Guido Cozzi/Fototeca 9x12 At the time, within the so-called New Sacristy of the Basilica of San Lorenzo in Florence (an architectural space conceived as a mausoleum for the Medici family), scaffolding was being erected under the watchful eye of Michelangelo Buonarroti. The artist, known to the world today as Michelangelo, was nearly 60 years old and had been commissioned to design the sacristy, which would mirror Filippo Brunelleschi’s Old Sacristy. But events overtook him. A few days earlier, he had left Florence for Rome, where he arrived on September 23, just two days before the pope’s death. pages.title: Michelangelo Used These Custom, Multi-Headed Brushes While Painting 'The Last Judgment' to Replicate His Intricate Sculpting Techniques
pages.description: While restoring the Sistine Chapel, researchers discovered wavy groupings of brushstrokes which indicated that the artist used the special brushes to create a distinct crosshatching pattern
pages.text: Michelangelo Used These Custom, Multi-Headed Brushes While Painting 'The Last Judgment' to Replicate His Intricate Sculpting Techniques Skip to main content Detail showing the hair of one of the figures around Christ in The Last Judgment , as example of the use of a multi-tipped brush Governatorato SCV – Direzione dei Musei e dei Beni Culturali This spring, the Vatican restored the Sistine Chapel for the first time in 30 years. Restorers worked for three months to remove layers of calcium lactate—a whitish salt from the dried sweat from millions of visitors and the plaster in the walls—that had settled onto Michelangelo ’s immaculate 16th-century murals. As experts climbed temporary scaffolding and applied distilled water and absorbent Japanese paper to clean away the grime, they got a rare, close-up view of Michelangelo’s vivid masterpieces. They noticed something unique about The Last Judgment , the massive mural located behind the chapel’s altar, as its original colors emerged. Michelangelo had painted with wavy brushstrokes that appeared to have moved in synchronization. “I initially saw that Michelangelo painted with parallel strokes, often perpendicular to each to give a cross-hatching effect,” Paolo Violini , the Vatican’s chief restorer, tells the London Times ’ Tom Kington. “Then I saw that when a stroke wobbled slightly, other strokes parallel to it had an identical wobble. That meant one thing: Michelangelo was using special brushes with multiple heads, each with a small brush on the end of it, allowing him to produce parallel strokes with one large brush.” Examp

pages.text: Michigan's Isle Royale National Park Is a camper's paradise | National Geographic National Geographic Traveller (UK) content straight to your inbox — sign up for our newsletter here TRAVEL Everything you should know about Isle Royale National Park Michigan’s remote and rugged Lake Superior archipelago—which encompasses nearly 450 islands—is a true Northwoods escape, ideal for hikers, wildlife lovers, and stargazers. In western Lake Superior, Isle Royale National Park is an archipelago comprised of over 400 smaller islands and rocky islets, including Siksiwit Island, Chippewa Harbor Islands, and Mott Island, the park’s summer headquarters on the south side of Rock Harbor Channel. Aaron Black-Schmidt, Tandem Stock By Amy S. Eckert Last updated March 31, 2026 • 13 min read Isle Royale National Park offers an unforgettable Lake Superior wilderness escape in Michigan . Despite its name, Isle Royale encompasses not merely its namesake island, but an archipelago of nearly 450 islands located 14 miles (22.5 km) from the nearest mainland. Once in the park, you’ll discover a landscape of rocky shoreline and basalt ridges covered with sugar maple, birch, and evergreen forest. The woods are carpeted with delicate wildflowers like bluebells, Canada Mayflowers, and lady’s slippers, and in late summer, you can harvest thimbleberries for snacking. If you’re lucky, you may spot moose, wolves, and aquatic birds along the park’s 165 miles (265 km) of hiking trails. The microloan program provides loans up to $50,000 to help small businesses and certain not-for-profit childcare centers start up and expand. The average microloan is about $13,000. SBA provides funds to specially designated intermediary lenders, which are nonprofit community-based organizations with experience in lending as well as management and technical assistance. These intermediaries administer the Microloan program for eligible borrowers. Am I eligible? To be eligible for a microloan, businesses must: Not be a type of ineligible business Be an operating business Operate for profit Be located in the U.S. Be small under SBA size requirements How do I use a microloan? Microloans can be used for a variety of purposes that help small businesses expand. Use them when you need less than $50,000 to start and/or grow your small business. A few weeks ago I wrote here about Wandering Around , a free browser game in which you can walk through any town or city on Earth, built on the fly from OpenStreetMap. Thanks to your comments and feedback, the game has now left beta: version 1.0 is live. Play it here: https://wanderingaround.games (phone and desktop, no download, no account needed) This post is about what changed on the OSM side since then. Buildings that look like the real thing Churches are built from their real outline. The game reads the shape of the building and finds the nave, the transepts and the choir, and each part gets its own roof that follows the shape. A square part that sticks out becomes the tower. A church mapped carefully as a cross shape now also looks like one at eye level. Mosques get a dome on a drum, pointed windows and a minaret. They are recognised by religion=muslim , building=mosque or the name. Cemeteries ( landuse=cemetery ) are laid out with gravel paths, rows of graves in neutral shapes, low hedges and trees. Sidewalks now run along the whole street as one continuous strip. Short gaps are filled and corners join neatly. Shop fronts, front doors and porches get their own place in the facade, so windows don’t end up behind a door. I’ve been building Wandering Around , a free browser game in which you can walk around any town or city on Earth. The whole world comes from OpenStreetMap, so I’d like to share how it uses OSM data and ask this community for feedback. Play it here: https://wanderingaround.games (works on phone and desktop, no account needed) News and updates: https://ko-fi.com/wanderingaroundtheworld Screenshots and a short video: https://mikehur.itch.io/wandering-around How the map is built Streets, buildings, water, parks and bridges come from OpenFreeMap vector tiles (zoom 14, OpenMapTiles schema). The game fetches the tiles around the player, decodes them in the browser, stitches buildings that are split across tile edges and turns everything back into OSM-style features with tags. The game logic works on those tags, so it is the same code whether the data comes from tiles or (as a fallback) from Overpass. 2D and 3D: the same data drives a 2D map and a 3D eye-level view. Building heights come from OSM where they are tagged. pages.text: Military and veteran retirement benefits | USAGov Skip to main content Military and veteran retirement benefits If you retire from a career in the military, you may be eligible for a pension. The plan and benefits you will receive depend on your situation. Pension plans for active duty military There are two pension plans for active duty service members. These include: The Legacy or High 36 Retirement System Blended Retirement System (BRS) Both plans require 20 or more years of service. The amount you receive from each plan is also based on the amount you earned from your basic pay and the date you joined the military. Find your basic pay amount based on your pay grade and the number of years you served. If you joined the military: Before January 1, 2006 - You are in the legacy/high 36 retirement system. Between Jan 1, 2006, and December 31, 2017 - You had a choice of keeping the legacy/high 36 or choosing the BRS. After December 31, 2017 - You are in the BRS. Determine your military pension plan and calculate your pay Legacy or High 36 Retirement System - This plan is based on an average of your highest 36 months of basic pay. The government does not match your contributions to the Thrift Savings plan. Blended Retirement System (BRS) - The government matches your contributions to the Thrift Savings Plan up to 4%. You will also receive a pension based on an average of your highest 36 months of basic pay. Use a military pension calculator to estimate retirement pay. Nimitz with his third Gold Star Chester William Nimitz Fleet Admiral, United States Navy Born: 1885 in Fredericksburg, Texas Died: 1966 in San Francisco Bay, California Buried: Golden Gate National Cemetery, San Bruno, California Significance: Admiral Nimitz was Commander in Chief, United States Pacific Fleet at the time of the Liberation of Guam and the attacks on Iwo Jima and Okinawa. After graduating from the Naval Academy in 1905, he served on various ships in the Pacific. On December 31, 1941 he assumed command of the Pacific Fleet. At the end of the war, his headquarters was at Fonte Plateau, now called Nimitz Hill, in Guam. In 1944 he was promoted to Fleet Admiral and served as Chief of Naval Operations. On September 2, 1945, Nimitz signed for the United States when Japan formally surrendered on board the Missouri in Tokyo Bay.
